# Sheet-only bot — Design Spec

**Date:** 2026-10-12
**Status:** Approved by the user in conversation ("approved … DONT STOP")
**Stack:** n8n workflow (generated by `build_workflow.py` / `deploy_graph.py`), Google Sheets, n8n Data Tables

---

## 1. Goal

Remove Postgres (Supabase) from the Telegram bot. The sheet is the only source of
truth the bot reads and writes; the bot no longer depends on a database that only
ever heard about its own writes.

## 2. Why

The admin edits the sheet by hand and never uses the dashboard, so the database
cannot stay current. The bot's lookups read the database, and every write goes to
the row number the database holds. That produced, on 2026-10-12:

- a payment written to the **wrong guest's row** (the database's stored `sheet_row`
  was one off after rows were inserted by hand), and
- stale totals: `paid = (database paid) + new payment` is written into the sheet's
  cumulative cell, so a stale database overwrites a correct sheet.

Reading the sheet in the same turn the bot writes it removes both.

## 3. Decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scope | Everything: sessions, lookups, mirror, reconcile. One deploy. |
| Sessions | n8n Data Table `bookings_bot_sessions` (still exists, same four columns), **proven with a scratch workflow before use**. If the proof fails, sessions stay on Postgres and the rest ships anyway (a recorded ruling). |
| Reading the sheet | The Sheets **API** through HTTP Request nodes (`values.get`), never the Sheets node: the repo documents that node as numbering rows wrongly. A row's number is its array index + 1. |
| `Brain` | Unchanged. The new Code nodes return rows in the shape the old SQL returned. |
| Data | Nothing is deleted. Supabase, `supabase/` and `webui/` stay in the repo, marked retired. |
| Rollback | The active version before the deploy is recorded; `restore_workflow_version` puts it back. |

## 4. Graph changes

| Before (Postgres) | After |
|---|---|
| `Load Session`, `Save Session`, `Clear Session` | Data Table nodes: `get` / `upsert` on `chat_id`. |
| `Read Bookings For Edit` (SQL) | `Fetch Bookings Formulas` + `Fetch Bookings Values` (HTTP `values.get` of `A1:U2000`, `FORMULA` and `UNFORMATTED_VALUE`) → `Read Bookings For Edit` (Code). |
| `Read Locations`, `Read Report Locations`, `Read Availability Locations` (SQL) | `Fetch … Locations` (HTTP `values.get` of the `الإتاحة` tab `A2:B2000`) → the same-named Code node returning `{الشقة, الغرفة}` rows. |
| `Read Next Booking ID` (SQL) | `Fetch Booking Ids` (HTTP, `B1:B2000`) → `Read Next Booking ID` (Code). |
| `Build Shadow Write`, `Shadow Write`, `Read Booking Id`, `Write Booking Id`, `Write Line Id`, `Write Snapshot`, `Read Discrepancies`, `Build Reconcile Message`, `Read Unmirrored Bookings`, `Append Mirror Row`, `Mark Mirrored` | Removed, with their IF/Code helpers and wiring. |

`Config` gains `AVAILABILITY_TAB` (`الإتاحة`). The Postgres credential becomes unused.

Every fetch that follows a node emitting many items (`Fetch Locations` after the
bookings lookup, `Fetch Booking Ids` after the registry) is `executeOnce`: an HTTP
node runs once per incoming item.

## 5. Reading a booking from the sheet (`Read Bookings For Edit`)

Input: the two `values.get` responses. Row `i` of `values` is sheet row `i + 1`;
row 1 holds the headers; trailing empty rows are trimmed by the API and interior
blanks are kept (as `[]`); short rows are padded.

A row is a **booking** when its `اسم المقيم` is non-empty and it is not a **line**.

A row is a **line** of the booking above it when all of these hold:

- it is directly under that booking's block (`row === block_end + 1`);
- `ID`, `اسم المقيم`, `اسم الشقة`, `رقم الغرفة` and `تاريخ البداية` are equal to the booking's;
- `اجمالي سعر الحجز` is blank;
- `اجمالي ما تم دفعه` or `طريقة الدفع` is filled.

That is exactly what `commitPaymentLine` writes (it copies the identity columns, leaves
the price blank and fills paid and method). A test pins the identity columns to
`LINE_IDENTITY_COLS` in `brain.js`. Column `معرف النظام` is not read.

Each booking is returned as one item with the sheet's own Arabic headers plus:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row_number` | The sheet row. |
| `booking_id` | The row number (an in-turn handle; nothing else reads a database id any more). |
| `lines` | `[{ seq, row, method, amount }]`, `seq` from 2, `amount` = the line's paid cell. |
| `block_end` | The last row the booking occupies (its own row, or its last line). |
| `total_is_formula` | `اجمالي سعر الحجز` is a formula that refers to the nights column (`=500*I10`, `=(650*I19)-2200`). Hand-typed constants (`=12900`, `=1400+700`) are not. |

Values: money and nights come from the values read (numbers stay numbers). An
open-ended stay (`عدد الليالي` is a formula starting `=TODAY()`) is `'=OPEN'`, as before.
Dates (`تاريخ البداية`, `تاريخ المغادرة`) are returned as `YYYY-MM-DD`: Sheets serial
numbers are converted, and `YYYY-MM-DD` / `d/m/yyyy` strings are normalised. `ID` is
returned as text (`'19**'`, `'31'`, or `''` when blank). Rows are returned in row order.

Carried-over guests (starred IDs, or no ID) are ordinary rows, so the bot's clash
check now sees them. If the read fails, the node returns no rows.

## 6. Next booking ID

`Read Next Booking ID` takes column B, folds Arabic-Indic digits, keeps only plain
counters (`^[0-9]{1,6}$`, so starred carry-overs and passport numbers are ignored) and
returns `{ next_booking_id: max + 1 }` (1 when there are none). The tab is a single
month, so "this month only" holds by construction. Cancelled bookings still count,
as before.

## 7. Registry

The `الإتاحة` tab, `A2:B`: row 2 is the header (`الشقة`, `الغرفة`), the junk row
`التاريخ` has no room and is skipped. Rooms keep the tab's order. `Brain` and both
report builders already read `الشقة` / `الغرفة` and tolerate a row without a room.

## 8. Sessions

Data Table `bookings_bot_sessions` (`chat_id`, `state`, `data`, `updated_at`).

- `Load Session`: `get` by `chat_id`, limit 1, `alwaysOutputData` (a chat with no row
  yields an empty item, which `Brain` reads as "no session").
- `Save Session` / `Clear Session`: `upsert` matching `chat_id`; `updated_at` is
  `Date.now()` (the same server clock `Brain` compares against).

History: this store was abandoned on 2026-08-14 because it "looked up cleanly and
wrote nothing". Before any of this is wired, a scratch workflow runs the exact
node parameters (upsert, read back, upsert again, read back, delete) and the rows
are checked through the data-table API. That scratch workflow also proves a new
HTTP Request node can be bound to the Google credential over MCP.

## 9. Deploy

1. Record the active version id.
2. Apply the migration to the **draft** (in batches of at most 90 operations, each
   atomic): add the new nodes, rewire, remove the retired nodes, swap the session
   nodes. `deploy_graph.py` is idempotent.
3. Verify the draft: no Postgres node, every `$('…')` reference resolves, `Brain`
   byte-identical to `brain.js`, the gate and wiring as designed, the Data Table
   and HTTP nodes carry their credentials.
4. Publish once. Watch the next executions for errors.

## 10. Tests

- Code nodes: offline, on fixtures taken from the real tab (the duplicate-id rows
  37–39, starred carry-overs, a row with no ID, formula totals), plus a round trip
  between what `commitPaymentLine` writes and what the reader parses.
- `Brain`: the existing suite, unchanged.
- Graph: no Postgres node anywhere in the built or merged workflow; sessions are Data
  Table nodes; fetches that follow multi-item nodes are `executeOnce`; the migration
  applied to a stripped copy of the old graph equals the built graph; the validator
  still passes.
- Parity: a read-only script runs the lookup on the live tab and prints what it finds.

## 11. Risks

- Each lookup turn does two Sheets API reads (a second or two). Always current.
- Line detection is structural; an unusual hand-made row could be misread. The parity
  script shows what the reader makes of the live tab.
- A row inserted between the lookup and the Confirm tap (seconds to minutes) is the
  only remaining wrong-row window. A write-time row check would close it and is not
  part of this change.
- The first message after deploy is the first real use of the Data Table and the
  HTTP reads together; rollback is one call.

## 12. Out of scope

Deleting Supabase, `supabase/` and `webui/`; removing the dead fields in `Brain`
(`bookingId`, `shiftFrom`, the payment-ledger object); the write-time row check.
